The surge current rating is inversely proportional to the square root of time for an SCR.  

For a half-cycle surge at 50 Hz:  
Half-cycle duration = \( \frac{1}{2 \times 50} = 0.01 \ \text{s} \)  
One-cycle duration = \( \frac{1}{50} = 0.02 \ \text{s} \)  

The relationship is:  
\[
I^2 t = \text{constant}
\]  
So:  
\[
I_{\text{1-cycle}} = I_{\text{half-cycle}} \times \sqrt{\frac{t_{\text{half}}}{t_{\text{full}}}}
\]  
\[
I_{\text{1-cycle}} = 3000 \times \sqrt{\frac{0.01}{0.02}}
\]  
\[
I_{\text{1-cycle}} = 3000 \times \sqrt{\frac{1}{2}} \approx 3000 \times 0.7071 \approx 2121.32 \ \text{A}
\]  

Final answer: (C)
